The [**detqc**](https://jakebrownscombe.github.io/detqc/) R package reads, checks and filters
detection files into a detection set; **detfield** positions the animals. This page reads the
files of the Stoney Lake example included with **detfield** with **detqc**'s readers, hands
the detection set to `bin_detections()` with `detqc::as_detfield_input()`, and computes the
hourly location surfaces. The example has five simulated animals and 70 receivers over 48
hours from 1 June 2024. A detection set that **detqc** has checked and filtered, such as its
own `detqc::stoney_clean`, is handed over the same way.

## Read the files into a detection set

The three files, detections, deployments and tags, are already in the column names the
positionR packages share, so the column map **detqc** reads them with names each column as
itself. A file in another layout takes a map from your column names to these; the OTN, GLATOS,
VUE and VDAT formats need none.

```{r column-maps}
# Attach detfield, and ggplot2 for the figures
library(detfield)
library(ggplot2)
# A column map that reads each named column as itself, with its type
same_names <- function(types) {
  data.frame(format = "glatos", target = names(types), source = names(types),
             sep = "", type = unname(types),
             tz = ifelse(types == "datetime", "UTC", ""), note = "")
}
same_names(c(datetime = "datetime", receiver_serial = "character"))
```

```{r read-files}
# Find a file included with detfield
in_file <- function(name) system.file("extdata", name, package = "detfield")
# Read the detections, the receiver deployments and the tags with detqc
detections <- detqc::read_detections(
  in_file("stoney_detections.csv"), format = "glatos",
  col_map = same_names(c(datetime = "datetime", receiver_serial = "character",
                         transmitter = "character", animal_id = "character"))
)
deployments <- detqc::read_deployments(
  in_file("stoney_deployments.csv"), format = "glatos",
  col_map = same_names(c(receiver_serial = "character",
                         station_id = "character",
                         deploy_datetime = "datetime",
                         recover_datetime = "datetime",
                         deploy_lat = "numeric", deploy_lon = "numeric",
                         deploy_z = "numeric"))
)
animals <- detqc::read_animals(
  in_file("stoney_tags.csv"), format = "glatos",
  col_map = same_names(c(transmitter = "character", animal_id = "character",
                         min_delay = "numeric", max_delay = "numeric"))
)
c(detections = nrow(detections), deployments = nrow(deployments),
  animals = nrow(animals))
```

`detqc::detset()` joins the three tables and gives each detection the station of the
deployment in the water when it was logged:

```{r detset}
# Build the detection set
dets <- detqc::detset(detections, deployments, animals)
dets
```

## Hand off

`detqc::as_detfield_input()` returns the three tables `bin_detections()` reads: the
detections, the listening table, and the tag delays from the animals table. A receiver counts
as listening in an hour when it was in the water and the listening audit of **detqc**, where
it has run, did not mark its day as not listening.

```{r hand-off}
# Export the detections, the listening table and the tag delays for detfield
detfield_input <- detqc::as_detfield_input(dets)
str(detfield_input, max.level = 1)
```

```{r bin}
# Count detections per animal, hour and listening receiver
hourly <- do.call(bin_detections, detfield_input)
table(unique(hourly[c("animal_id", "bin_start")])$animal_id)
```

The field is built from the lake raster and the deployments of the detection set, which keep
`deploy_lat`, `deploy_lon` and `deploy_z`, with the Stoney stand-in curve, the curve the
detections were simulated from. A study with its own range test reads its fitted model here, as
[Range models: bring your own, or start from two distances](range-model.html) shows.

```{r field}
# Read the lake and measure distances through water from the deployments
lake <- terra::rast(in_file("stoney_depth.tif"))
distances <- water_distances(lake, dets$deployments)
# Build the field from the stand-in curve, with no spread between hours
curve <- de_logistic(d50 = c(250, 750), d05 = c(500, 1500), depth = c(1, 35))
field <- de_field(distances, de_model(curve, sigma = list(station_hour = 0)))
```

`location_surface()` gives each detected hour a probability over the water cells
([the model](positioning.html#the-model)):

```{r surfaces}
# Compute one surface per animal and detected hour
surface <- location_surface(hourly, field)
surface
```

## Hours by receivers heard

How well an hour is placed depends first on how many receivers heard the animal in it.

```{r heard-by}
# Count the receivers that heard each animal in each hour, three or more
# together
heard <- hourly[hourly$y > 0, ]
heard_by <- aggregate(list(receivers = heard$station_id,
                           detections = heard$y),
                      by = heard[c("animal_id", "bin_start")],
                      FUN = function(v) if (is.numeric(v)) sum(v) else length(v))
heard_by$heard_by <- factor(pmin(heard_by$receivers, 3), 1:3,
                            c("1", "2", "3 or more"))
# Tabulate the hours per animal
hours_table <- table(heard_by$animal_id, heard_by$heard_by)
hours_table
round(mean(heard_by$receivers == 1), 2)
```

```{r heard-by-plot, fig.height = 3, fig.alt = "Stacked bars of detected hours per animal by the number of receivers that heard it; most hours of four animals were heard by two receivers or more, and stoney-04's mostly by one."}
# Plot the detected hours of each animal by the receivers that heard it
ggplot(heard_by, aes(animal_id, fill = heard_by)) +
  geom_bar() +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(name = "Receivers\nthat heard\nthe animal",
                       option = "magma", begin = 0.3, end = 0.85) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Detected hours") +
  theme_positionr()
```

*Detected hours of each simulated animal on the 70 receivers (`r nrow(heard_by)` hours in
all).*

`r round(100 * mean(heard_by$receivers == 1))`% of the detected hours are single-receiver
hours, `r sum(heard_by$receivers == 1 & heard_by$animal_id == "stoney-04")` of them
`stoney-04`'s in the north-west arm, where one receiver covers most of the water. On the
20-receiver array of `detqc::stoney_clean`, about 1.3 km between receivers, most detected hours
are heard by one receiver, so the array's spacing sets how many hours are placed well. [Hourly positions against the true
track](positioning.html) measures the error of the hourly positions for each count of
receivers.

## One hour of each kind

`stoney-01` is the first animal with hours of all three kinds. For each kind, its hour with
the most detections is drawn with the true path of the hour from the simulation:

```{r pick-hours}
# Pick stoney-01's hour with the most detections for each count of receivers
st01 <- heard_by[heard_by$animal_id == "stoney-01", ]
picked <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(st01, st01$heard_by), function(kind) {
  kind[which.max(kind$detections), ]
}))
picked[c("bin_start", "receivers", "detections")]
# The true path of each picked hour, one position a minute
true_path <- function(hour_start) {
  track <- detfield::stoney_track$track
  track[track$animal_id == "stoney-01" & track$datetime >= hour_start &
          track$datetime <= hour_start + 3600, ]
}
# The map window: 1.7 km square on the cell holding the hour's mean true
# position, with its edges on cell edges
around <- function(path, half = 850) {
  centre <- terra::xyFromCell(lake, terra::cellFromXY(lake,
                                                      cbind(mean(path$x),
                                                            mean(path$y))))
  c(centre[1] + c(-half, half), centre[2] + c(-half, half))
}
```

The hour heard by the most receivers first:

```{r hour-many, fig.height = 4.8, fig.alt = "Location surface of stoney-01 for an hour heard by four receivers: a compact patch between them, with the hour's true path running through it."}
# Map the hour heard by three or more receivers, with its true path
many_hour <- picked$bin_start[picked$heard_by == "3 or more"]
many_path <- true_path(many_hour)
plot(surface, animal_id = "stoney-01", bin_start = many_hour,
     ext = around(many_path)) +
  geom_path(data = many_path, aes(x, y), colour = "white", linewidth = 1.1,
            inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  geom_path(data = many_path, aes(x, y), colour = "grey45", linewidth = 0.5,
            inherit.aes = FALSE)
```

*Location surface of `stoney-01` for the hour from
`r format(many_hour, "%H:%M UTC on %e June 2024", tz = "UTC")`, heard by
`r picked$receivers[picked$heard_by == "3 or more"]` receivers, with the true path of the hour
(line, one position a minute).*

```{r hour-two, fig.height = 4.8, fig.alt = "Location surface of stoney-01 for an hour heard by two receivers: a band of cells between the two, crossed by the hour's true path."}
# Map the hour heard by two receivers, with its true path
two_hour <- picked$bin_start[picked$heard_by == "2"]
two_path <- true_path(two_hour)
plot(surface, animal_id = "stoney-01", bin_start = two_hour,
     ext = around(two_path)) +
  geom_path(data = two_path, aes(x, y), colour = "white", linewidth = 1.1,
            inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  geom_path(data = two_path, aes(x, y), colour = "grey45", linewidth = 0.5,
            inherit.aes = FALSE)
```

*Location surface of `stoney-01` for the hour from
`r format(two_hour, "%H:%M UTC on %e June 2024", tz = "UTC")`, heard by two receivers, with
the hour's true path.*

With two receivers the surface is a band of cells between the two that heard the animal.

```{r hour-one, fig.height = 4.8, fig.alt = "Location surface of stoney-01 for a single-receiver hour: probability spread round the one receiver that heard it, with the hour's true path inside it."}
# Map the single-receiver hour, with its true path
one_hour <- picked$bin_start[picked$heard_by == "1"]
one_path <- true_path(one_hour)
plot(surface, animal_id = "stoney-01", bin_start = one_hour,
     ext = around(one_path)) +
  geom_path(data = one_path, aes(x, y), colour = "white", linewidth = 1.1,
            inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  geom_path(data = one_path, aes(x, y), colour = "grey45", linewidth = 0.5,
            inherit.aes = FALSE)
```

*A single-receiver hour: the location surface of `stoney-01` for the hour from
`r format(one_hour, "%H:%M UTC on %e June 2024", tz = "UTC")`, heard by one receiver
(`r picked$detections[picked$heard_by == "1"]` of
`r hourly$n[hourly$animal_id == "stoney-01" & hourly$bin_start == one_hour][1]`
transmissions), with the hour's true path.*

One receiver's count says how far from it the animal probably was and nothing about the
direction, so the surface spreads round that receiver as far as the silent receivers beyond it
allow.

## Two errors at the hand-off

**The animals table has no delays.** Without `min_delay` and `max_delay`,
`as_detfield_input()` says so and returns no tag delays, and `bin_detections()` stops:

```{r no-delays}
# Drop the delay columns from the animals table, and hand off again
no_delays <- dets
no_delays$animals <- dets$animals[, setdiff(names(dets$animals),
                                            c("min_delay", "max_delay"))]
try(do.call(bin_detections, detqc::as_detfield_input(no_delays)))
```

Read the tag specification sheet with `detqc::read_tag_specs()` and pass it to
`detqc::read_animals()`, or give the delay to `bin_detections()` as `tag_delay = c(120, 180)`.

**The listening table is not a deployments table.** `detfield_input$listening` is a list of
two tables and has no positions, so `water_distances()` stops:

```{r listening-not-deployments}
# Try the listening table in place of the deployments
try(water_distances(lake, detfield_input$listening))
```

Give `water_distances()` the deployments of the detection set, `dets$deployments`, as above.
